about: The one source of the films' sound (ADR-014). The values are docs/notes/sound-2026-09/SPEC.md's, chosen by ear and by measurement over six rounds; each block names the section it comes from.

`make sound` (www/brand/sound.py) writes the marks' and the bed's scores into www/video/sound/ (the notes from the score each names under docs/notes/sound-2026-09/scores/, the cast from here) and the mix's defaults into www/video/tools/sound_defaults.py. `make dev-check` fails when a generated file is stale, a cast preset is not in the bank, or a number is a film tool's level default or a pipeline's fallback for it: mix.py reads the bed's level and duck from the ladder (`ladder.bed_rest_lu`) and the duck (`duck.broadband_db`), and app_audio.py the app's gain from `before_the_grammar`.

Strings are prose. Every number and pitch is either written into a generated file, or describes the record scores' notes and is checked against them by `--check` (the pedal, the marks' length, the lead's legato and swell, the bed's voicings, burble and sighs, and the demo), so a change here that the scores do not make fails the check. The `stock` knob values are checked against the bank by test_sound.py's render test.

Units: knob values are the engine's normalized knob values, the ones a score's `params` take. Pitches are as they sound. LUFS is ITU-R BS.1770-4, as www/video/tools/mix.py computes it. A pan is -1 (left) to +1 (right), the score renderer's equal-power pan.

Two things are stand-ins, marked `stand_in`, that a film made to this must replace: the demo and the lead's bend for portamento. The bed's sighs, placed by hand in the audition, are placed by www/video/tools/fit_score.py --film (`bed.parts.melody.placement`).

key.mode: F Lydian for the cycle's first half (G6/F carries the B natural); minor color in its second half (Bbm6/F carries the Db)

tempo.about: SPEC section 1. A beat at 66 BPM is 0.909 s and a bar 3.636 s. The marks are written at 60 BPM, so a beat is a second, and are placed into the 66 BPM grid by time.

form.length: The cycle repeats for as long as the film needs. The drone is held, never re-struck, and the pad's ties carry across cycles.
film: The bed sounds from the first frame (its drone first), and the entrance mark (Bloom) comes in `bed_first.entrance_after_beats` later, blooms into the bed, and the first word follows it closely.
Narration, with demos in the grammar (`grammar`).
The exit mark (Reach) follows the last word closely and resolves to F.
form.motif: The motif plays only as the two marks. The bed never quotes it: not its head, its sequence or a variant.

bed_first.about: Chosen by the maintainer on 2026-10-07, watching the launch film: the bed (the drone) sounds from the film's first frame, under the opening's waveform, so what is seen is what is heard; Bloom follows a moment later. It was silence, then the bed and Bloom together. The entrance is two of the bed's beats in (1.82 s at 66 BPM), set on the grid (the drone articulates no bar before it), and the drone opens with `marks.drone_fade_in`, short enough that there is no silence.

cast.about: SPEC section 2. Every note is a bank preset played by the engine. `knobs` are the tweaks the finals used, each with the preset's stock value; every other knob is stock. The generator writes each part's preset, voices, trim, transpose and `used` knobs, the lead's `bend` times and the drone's `breath` into every track of the scores that plays it. The lead's `legato` and `swell` are checked against the scores, and the demo against the reel it played in.

shortlist.about: The sixteen presets a film casts from, shortlisted in round 2 by a two-note probe of all 62 bank presets (RFC-007 part 2; SPEC section 2, 'Measured for casting'). Bells, tines and plucks are excluded by name.

criteria.note: Also a low spectral centroid, a round attack, nothing above 4 kHz worth naming, and no energy below 60 Hz worth naming (under 0.02%). White noise measures a noise share of 0.70.

room.about: SPEC section 5, 'One room'. Only Cathedral exposes a reverb in this cast, and every Cathedral part shares these stock settings. Wobble Board, Held Under and Solo Flight have no reverb node and sit dry in front of it. No outside reverb.

drone.role: The floor: F2 and C3, held for the whole piece.

breath.about: The cutoff breathes once per cycle, lowest at the cycle's start: stock plus and minus 10%. The generator writes `low` and `high` over the bed score's own automation points.

bed_pad.role: The bed's chord pad, two bars a chord, voice-led.

marks_pad.role: The marks' pad, under the lead.

amp#attack.effect: 10-90% rise 0.30 s, so a half-second chord can speak

lead.role: The motif's one voice everywhere it plays (the marks), and the bed's melody. Two voices per note; one track per note.

amp#sustain.effect: Holds 4.1 dB under its attack (6.4 dB at 0.70)

amp#release.effect: Note-off to -30 dB in 0.11 s (0.025-0.030 s at 0.30)

bend.stand_in: Portamento: each note bends in from the previous pitch with the score's `pitch_drop` (semis = previous minus current), because the score example cannot set the instrument's glide.

legato.about: Each note is held into the next. SPEC says 0.06 beat, written at the marks' 60 BPM, where a beat is a second; the bed's record holds 0.066 beat at 66 BPM, the same 0.06 s.

swell.about: A line's last note swells by a fader from its onset.

release.about: Measured: from note-off to -30 dB in 0.108-0.112 s, for all 18 of the motif's notes in the finals (SPEC section 10). A film's sighs are placed so that this tail has ended before the next line.

burble.role: The bed's low burble. Transposed +12 because it sounds an octave below the key.

demo.role: The instrument played between lines. No generated score plays it; it is the reel's `demo` track, which `--check` compares with this.
demo.stand_in: The demo is the engine playing a score, not the app recorded, and its 'Bright' gesture is the cutoff automated.

marks.about: SPEC section 3. Each mark's score is the record named in `score`; the generator writes it to `out` with the cast from `cast`, mapping each track to a part by `tracks` (a trailing * matches any suffix). `length_s` is checked against the records; it, the marks' levels and the numbers in `into_the_bed` and `out_of_the_bed` are written into sound_defaults.py (`MARKS`).
marks.in_a_film: The lead and the marks' pad are scaled together so the mark's 4.5 s, with the drone and anything under it, is the ladder's `marks_lufs`.

bloom.title: Bloom
bloom.harmony: Fmaj9 | G6/F, the Lydian B | Fmaj9 without E4, so E5 is alone on top. It ends open, on the major 7th.

into_the_bed.held: Bloom's last chord (A3 C4 G4) is the bed's bar 1: those notes stay on the marks' pad until a voice moves (A3 and C4 at bar 3, G4 at bar 5). The bed pad plays only the voices that move.

reach.title: Reach
reach.harmony: Fmaj7 | Bbmaj9/F (the C5 is its 9th) | Bbm6/F (the sigh under the held C5) | Fmaj7: I IV iv I.

out_of_the_bed.hand_over: The bed's voices end on Reach's downbeat, each stepping to the nearest note of Reach's Fmaj7 (A3 C4 E4), so the hand-over takes about a beat on the bed's release, wherever the bed is in its cycle.
out_of_the_bed.passing_chord: If a hand-over would be abrupt, one passing chord of a beat or two, voice-led.
out_of_the_bed.drone: Continues, and is released with Reach.
out_of_the_bed.hold: No chord change in the bar before Reach's downbeat: the bed holds its chord into the hand-over. In the reel the bed came back from the demo on G6/F and held it to Reach, rather than strike Bbmaj7/F 1.8 s before Reach's downbeat (a 2-beat Bbmaj7/F re-struck there never bloomed, and dipped 5 dB).

bed.about: SPEC section 4: N3. The score is the record named in `score`, three cycles with one sigh; the generator writes it to `out` with the cast from `cast`. `parts` describes its notes (the drone's pitches, the pad's voicings, the burble, the sighs) and is checked against them, so a change here fails the check until the score makes it too. They are also written into sound_defaults.py (`BED`), which www/video/tools/fit_score.py --film writes a film's bed from: the cycle held and tied for as long as the film needs, around its demos and marks, with the sighs in the narration's gaps. Each part's EQ, pan and level is in `mix.parts`.
bed.name: N3
bed.title: N3

drone.held: For the whole piece, never re-struck, its cutoff breathing once a cycle (`cast.parts.drone.breath`).

pad.restrike: Only voices that move are re-struck (soft attack); the rest are tied, not re-struck. The inner lines descend chromatically (B, Bb, A and D, Db, C), and the top goes G G A G.

under_demo.about: SPEC section 9, rules 3 and 5. In the pause before a demo the pad is re-voiced to `voicing` on `on` (the marks' pad, whose 0.30 s rise speaks within the 0.7 s pause) and held until the bed comes back after the demo's note-off; the burble plays `counts_as`'s cell under it. With the demo's notes it makes `counts_as`, so the cycle resumes on the chord after it. In the reel the pad went to A3 C4, so the demo's F3 E4 G4 A4 completed an Fmaj9 without doubling it, and the bed came back on G6/F. No chord is struck less than `hold_before_s` before a demo's pause: the previous chord holds into it. The bed's pad takes 2.2 s to rise (`cast.parts.bed_pad`), so a chord struck later would never bloom, and a sliver of one would set the burble's cell going again for a note or two, a flam against the demo's own cell. In the reel Bbmaj7/F was struck 2.22 s before the pause. If the bed would come back inside the bar before the exit mark (`marks.reach.out_of_the_bed.hold_bars`), it does not: this voicing and the burble's cell carry on to the exit mark's downbeat, and nothing sounds past it.

burble.cell: Dotted eighths cycling a three-note cell (low, high, middle). The cell restarts at each chord change; the last note before a change is shortened to fit.

velocity.note: 0.5 x (1 + 0.1 sin(2 pi k / 7)): it breathes +/-10%, with no accents.

melody.placed: By www/video/tools/fit_score.py --film, by `placement`. In the audition they were placed by hand: one sigh in the narration clip, on the first chord change after its last line ended (0.16 s after it), and none in the reel, whose narration leaves no gap that holds one.
melody.shape: Falling two-note sighs on chord tones: a dotted quarter, then a held note, the second swelling.
melody.where: Only in the narration's gaps, never in the bar before the exit mark. A sigh that has no gap is skipped, not crowded.
melody.no_doubling: Where a sigh would double the pad, the pad's top voice rests and returns at its next move.

placement.about: The rule, derived from where the hand-placed sighs sat. A sigh starts on a chord change (the first downbeat of a chord's two bars) in a gap of the narration: at least `after_line_s` after a line ends, with the whole sigh (its two notes, then the lead's release to -30 dB, `cast.parts.lead.release`) over at least `before_line_s` before the next line starts. Never in a demo's slot (its line's end to the bed's return), never in a mark, and never in the `bars_before_exit` bars before the exit mark. Every chord change that holds a whole sigh gets one; one with no room is skipped, not crowded. Where a sigh's note is one the bed's pad is sounding, that voice rests from the sigh to the next chord change, where it is struck again.

mix.about: SPEC section 5, on stems. Filters are 2nd-order Butterworth, applied causally. Band splits for dynamic moves are zero-phase 4th-order and complementary, so they reconstruct exactly. Levels are re-checked after the EQ: drone, burble and melody against the pad, integrated over the bed (the melody: momentary median while it sounds).

sounding.about: What `while it sounds` means, where a part is levelled against the pad sounding with it (the melody; the marks' lead) and where a demo window is checked for sound: momentary loudness (400 ms blocks, 100 ms apart) above `part_lufs`, with the pad above `pad_lufs`. These are the audition's own gates (its build scripts measured every `while it sounds` this way).

drone.note: The low-pass is at 200 Hz because the partial that beats against the pad's B3 and Db4 is F2's third harmonic, at 262 Hz.

pad.about: Under speech, the pad dips further (`duck.pad_dip`).

voice_chain.about: SPEC section 6. The narration stem passes through these stages in order, then is normalized to the ladder's `narration_lufs`. The voice is Kokoro af_heart (RFC-004). Peaking filters are RBJ.

stages.note: When the 250-400 Hz power density exceeds 500-800 Hz by more than 3 dB. It measured 3.5-4.8 dB on every narration used.

Split band: a 4th-order zero-phase high-pass, the rest untouched. The threshold is the 95th percentile of speech frames, which measured -25.3 to -26.9 dBFS at -18 LUFS. Measured activity: 6.9-9.8% of frames.

ladder.about: SPEC section 7. `bed_rest_lu` is against the narration (so -21 LUFS) and `bed_under_demo_lu` against the demo (about -27 LUFS); the bed under speech is the duck (`duck`). The demos were -18 LUFS with the bed 9 LU under them until 2026-10-07, when the maintainer heard the launch film's Bright and Offer demos as a bit too loud: they are 3 dB down, the bed under them where it was. No cues: no whoosh, blip, shimmer or logo sting, and nothing in their place.

duck.about: SPEC section 8. Three moves on the bed under the voice, sharing one detector and one follower. The app's sound is not ducked: in this grammar the instrument never plays under the narration.

before_the_grammar.about: A film laid out before the grammar (its timeline has neither `marks` nor `demos`: a script still on Study or Signal) is mixed exactly as it was before ADR-014, so nothing about it changes until it is re-voiced onto the grammar (Plan-006 task 8). The voice is untreated at the ladder's `narration_lufs`. The bed, as one sound, sits `bed_db` under it and ducks `duck_db` broadband under the voice, with no carve and no dip. The app's recorded sound plays at `app_gain_db` (tools/app_audio.py's --gain-db, walkthrough.sh's APP_DB) and ducks `app_duck_db`, half the bed's duck, on the same detector and follower. The only change is that no cue is laid. These are the levels the films were mixed with before ADR-014 (they were mix_now). A film on the grammar lays its demos after its lines instead, each at the ladder's `demo_lufs`, and never ducks the app.

grammar.about: SPEC section 9: the rules a film follows. `reel` is the value the final reel used, and the one www/video/tools/timeline.py lays a film out on. `exit_ring_out_s` is how long a film runs after the exit mark's last note, for the room to ring out: the reel's end (42.62 s) came 2.6 s after Reach's last note (40.02 s). A demo's tail is measured, not assumed: its playing level is the median of the RMS of the mono sum (the two channels' mean) over `demo_tail_hop_s` frames between its first note and its last note-off, and the tail ends at the first frame after the note-off that is `demo_tail_db` under that level. The reel measured its stand-in demo this way at 1.08 s (it had assumed 1.12 s).
rules: The motif plays only as the two marks.
The first word comes 1.5-2 s after the entrance mark's last note. The bed (the mark's last chord held on) carries the gap and does not wait for a bar or cycle boundary.
The voice explains; 0.7 s after its last word the demo starts, wherever the bed is. If a re-strike would dip under the demo, the pad is re-voiced in the pause rather than waiting.
The demo is never cut off: its notes ring out on their own release. If it must end sooner, its playing ends sooner.
The voice waits until the demo's tail has fallen 30 dB under its playing level, then 0.8 s more on the bed, then continues. The bed returns over 1.0 s from note-off and resumes its cycle.
The exit mark enters 1.5-2 s after the last word ends, wherever the bed is, handing over as in `marks.reach`.
